ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled P(f), the horizontal axis is labeled f/R_b, and the horizontal-axis ticks include -2, -1, 0, 1, 2. The power spectral density curve has a main lobe centered at 0 at zero frequency, zeros appear at about f/R_b=±1, and afterward there are sidelobes near ±1 to ±2; at the same time, at the f=0 position there is also an upward impulse-like vertical arrow. Reasoning: The problem states that R_b is the bit rate of a binary digital PAM baseband signal. The spectral zeros appear at ±R_b, which matches the sinc^2-type spectrum produced by rectangular NRZ pulses with duration T_b; and the impulse component at f=0 indicates that this code type has a nonzero mean value, i.e. a DC component exists. In binary NRZ, the typical code type with nonzero mean and a DC component is unipolar NRZ. Therefore this signal likely uses the Unipolar NRZ line code.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the PSD P(f) has a main lobe centered at zero frequency, zeros at approximately f/R_b = ±1, side lobes beyond those zeros, and an impulse-like vertical arrow at f=0. Then use the question text to note that R_b is the bit rate for a binary digital PAM baseband signal. Match the visual PSD to known line-code spectra: zeros at ±R_b imply a rectangular NRZ pulse of width T_b, and the DC impulse implies the waveform has nonzero average value. The binary NRZ code with nonzero mean is Unipolar NRZ.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This uses direct spectral-shape identification: the rectangular-pulse sinc-squared envelope plus a DC spectral line uniquely indicate unipolar NRZ among common binary PAM line codes.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the plotted PSD as a continuous sinc-squared-like spectrum centered at f=0, with nulls at normalized frequencies about ±1, ±2 in units of R_b, and a distinct impulse/arrow at f=0 indicating a discrete DC component.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the statement that the plotted spectrum is for a binary digital PAM baseband signal and that R_b denotes bit rate, so normalized null locations can be interpreted relative to the bit interval T_b=1/R_b.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For binary PAM, an NRZ rectangular pulse of duration T_b has a sinc-squared power spectrum with first nulls at ±R_b. A unipolar code has nonzero mean, producing a discrete DC component at f=0; polar NRZ would lack the DC line, and RZ variants would have different null spacing. Therefore the code is unipolar NRZ.
